selected_result: Rump Theorem 3.5 and equation (3.11): a sharp, computable recursive-sum error bound using the unit in the first place of a concurrently computed absolute-value sum

bibliographic_source.title: Error Estimation of Floating-Point Summation and Dot Product
bibliographic_source.venue: BIT Numerical Mathematics 52 (2012), 201–220; author preprint accepted 2011

paper_locations.anchor: Binary floating-point format F, rounding to nearest, u, and ufp definition
Concurrent recursive sums of signed inputs and absolute inputs in the same given order
Error bounded by (n−1)u·ufp(S_hat_n), then by (n−1)u·S_hat_n; claimed sharpness for all n

task_clarification: For each positive n and representable input vector p, compute s_hat by recursive summation and S_hat by recursive summation of |p_i| in the same order, as Algorithm 3.2 specifies.

Formalize both inequalities in (3.11): |s_hat−Σ_i p_i| ≤ (n−1)u·ufp(S_hat) ≤ (n−1)u·S_hat. For nonzero r, ufp(r) is the source's largest binary power of two not exceeding |r|; the source explicitly defines ufp(0)=0, which covers all-zero inputs.

The labelled theorem also says the estimation is sharp for all n. Preserve that uniform-in-n attainability assertion. The source's witness p_1=1, p_i=u for i≥2 uses IEEE ties-to-even and yields s_hat=S_hat=1 with equality in the first bound; this does not assert sharpness separately for every possible tie rule or every observed pair.
scope_constraints: Do not replace the concurrently computed S_hat with the exact sum of |p_i|, or permit a different summation order for this theorem.
Do not add an n*u smallness guard; the theorem expressly holds without it in the stated no-overflow setting and allows underflow.
Use source-equivalent round-to-nearest binary floating-point semantics. Do not assume the target error bound as part of a format or operation interface.
Do not omit either displayed inequality or the theorem's sharpness sentence.

The paper permits arbitrary nearest-rounding tie rules for the inequalities, while its displayed sharpness witness uses ties-to-even. Do not silently conflate those quantifiers or require equality for every fixed tie rule.

Independent source review must document the paper's use of an absolute-value monotonicity step that may fail under asymmetric tie rules; do not silently strengthen the rounding assumptions to repair the printed proof.
